’Twas snurglic, and the vorghy quibbs
      Did skithe and wammle in the drale:
All flimty were the kittipoos,
      And the fenly glorps undersnarked.

“Beware the Snatterwock, my son!
      The jaws that bite, the claws that catch!
Beware the Murmurm bird, and shun
      The glarnious Clatterquatch!”

He took his zarbly sword in hand;
      Long time the grindsome foe he sought—
So rested he by the Bimbim tree
      And stood awhile in thought.

And, as in yarnish thought he stood,
      The Snatterwock, with eyes of flame,
Came snuffling through the murklig wood,
      And chundled as it came!

One, two! One, two! And through and through
      The zarbly blade went snicker-snack!
He left it dead, and with its head
      He went trompheling back.

“And hast thou slain the Snatterwock?
      Come to my arms, my gleamish boy!
O splendous day! Hurroon! Hurray!”
      He snorkled in his joy.

’Twas snurglic, and the vorghy quibbs
      Did skithe and wammle in the drale:
All flimty were the kittipoos,
      And the fenly glorps undersnarked.
